title: When a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure
body: Economist Charles Goodhart observed in 1975 that statistics used to steer policy tend to break down once people start aiming at them, because behaviour shifts to hit the number rather than the goal behind it. The snappy one-line version comes from anthropologist Marilyn Strathern. Examples are everywhere: a call centre judged on call length may rush customers off the phone, and a school judged on test scores may teach to the test.
